target: corolla (PO_0009059) as part of a qualified whole (pattern 12): whole flower (PO_0009046) with male (PATO_0000384)

target: corona lobe (FLOPO_0986035) part of staminal corona (FLOPO_0985022); '5 dents' is a count of corona lobes
reason: French 'couronne staminale' (stamen crown) with teeth: the teeth are lobes of the staminal corona. If the floras mean a toothed staminal tube (Meliaceae), the target would be the distal teeth of staminal tube FLOPO_0986013. Check against the source family.

target: grooved (PATO_0002255) / furrowed (PATO_0001948) of the stem or fruit; the number is a count of grooves, read like the counted part 'rib'
reason: French for a groove or flute on the surface ('rameaux 5-6-cannelés'). It is a surface feature of the organ, expressed by a PATO surface quality with a count. It is not an organ.

target: hypanthium (PO_0009065), proximal region (the part enclosing and adnate to the inferior ovary)
reason: Combretaceae usage: 'lower receptacle' is the part of the floral tube around the ovary, and 'upper receptacle' is the cup above it. This is the proximal region of the hypanthium, not the flower receptacle PO_0009064.

target: shoot axis (PO_0025029)

target: branch (PO_0025073)

target: lenticel (PO_0000031)
reason: Exact: the part is lenticel. 'present' is the quality that got merged into the noun phrase.

target: flower bud (PO_0000056) with state male (PATO_0000384), pattern 04
reason: A flower bud of a male flower. The sex is a state of the flower (pattern 04), and the shape, size and apiculate apex belong to the bud.

target: seed (PO_0009010), apex region; the seed is beaked (FLOPO:0991028), and length, shape and hairiness are qualities of the apex
reason: A beak is the prolonged apex of the seed. A region rule plus the existing 'beaked' value covers it, so it does not need a sibling of fruit beak FLOPO_0986139 for two floras.

target: epicalyx segment (FLOPO_0986038)
reason: Narrower or related: segments alternating with the sepals (Lythraceae, Rosaceae) are epicalyx segments or calyx appendages. 'present' and 'persistent' fit that class.

target: staminode (PO_0009077)
reason: Exact in use: the text itself glosses it as 'sterile filaments (staminodes) 3'.

target: bracteole (PO_0009043) with connate (FLOPO:0991067); the cups are counted as connate bracteole pairs
reason: A cup formed by fused, '2-toothed' bracteoles below the flower. The fused-bracteole pattern expresses it, and the counts are of these units. Not the Fagaceae cupule FLOPO_0986036.

target: surface of the spore (plant spore PO_0025017) or pollen (PO_0025281) wall, with clavate (PATO_0001883) sculpture
reason: Clavae are club-shaped ornament elements of the spore or pollen wall. Their shape is a sculpture quality of the wall surface, so no anatomy class is needed.
Fragment of the quality 'foliaceous' (leaf-like) from 'the 1-2 foliaceous ones' or 'foliaceous bracts'. The counted part is the bract named nearby.
A surface marking pattern (concentric striae or arcs on a seed, fruit or spore surface), not a structure. It is a surface quality of the organ named in context.

target: leaf rachis (PO_0020055) winged (FLOPO_0985004); the wing's width and shape are qualities of the wing as counted part ('winged' -> wing)
reason: 'rhachis' is an exact synonym on PO_0020055. A rachis wing is the leaf-rachis counterpart of petiole lamina (PO_0025129). The winged-part rule expresses it, so it does not need a new class.

target: calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), base region; the lobe is clawed (FLOPO:0991169)
reason: A claw is the narrowed stalk-like base of a perianth part. 'clawed' already exists as a value, and the base region carries length, width, channelled and pilose.

reason: Bryophyte or algal cell descriptions. The cell wall is a GO cellular component, not a PO organ, so it is a part of the cell class.

target: flower nectary (PO_0009056)
reason: Narrower: scale-like floral nectaries at the base of the carpels (Crassulaceae) or petals. Their shape and size are qualities of the nectary.

target: phyllome margin (PO_0025018), on the dorsal side
reason: Leafy liverworts and Selaginella describe the dorsal and ventral margins of their leaves separately. This is a margin region at a side position of the leaf (phyllome), not a class.

reason: Teeth of a phyllome (stipule, leaf, bract) that bear glands. The tooth class plus the glandular quality covers it, and counts are tooth counts.
